name: Damon self-ligating braces

lead: Damon braces are orthodontic brackets that hold the archwire with a built-in sliding door instead of rubber ties. People choose them for straighter teeth and a broader, fuller-looking smile, and the system is marketed for expanding the arch without extractions.

The passive clip lets the wire slide with little friction, so teeth move under lighter forces as the wire shape guides alignment. Systematic reviews describe lower friction as the most consistent advantage, with mixed findings on treatment time, comfort and hygiene. Looksmax forum users credit the system with arch expansion and, in some posts, jaw changes; no trials show facial-bone change from the bracket type.

paras: Treatment is run by an orthodontist as a standard course of braces: brackets bonded to the teeth, a series of archwires, and regular adjustment visits over many months. Users typically pair it with a retainer afterwards to hold the result.

Risks are those of braces generally: tooth soreness, mouth irritation, decalcification or decay if cleaning is poor, and relapse without a retainer. Reviews do not link the bracket type to extra hygiene problems. Claims of jaw or maxilla change have not been studied.

angle.text: The payoff people want is a straighter, fuller smile. Self-ligating brackets move the teeth under light forces, broadening the arch and aligning them, and forum users credit the system with extra arch expansion. Reviews report lower friction as the main documented advantage.

lead: Damon braces are a line of self-ligating orthodontic brackets, which hold the archwire with a built-in sliding door instead of elastic ties. The Damon SL1 was introduced in 1996 and is classed as a passive self-ligating system.[1] Manufacturers and some orthodontists say the design reduces friction and allows lighter forces, and the system is often marketed for arch expansion without extractions.

On looksmax.org, Damon braces are discussed as a way to widen the dental arch, improve the smile and, according to some posters, support jaw development. Published reviews describe a more modest picture: friction is the most consistently reported advantage in laboratory conditions, while claims about faster treatment, comfort and hygiene are mixed or unsupported.[1]

paras: Self-ligating brackets are typically stainless steel, though ceramic and polycarbonate versions exist, and are divided into passive types, where the door applies no pressure on the wire, and active types, where a clip presses on it. Damon brackets are passive.[1] Advocates cite fewer elastic ties, a smaller appearance and shorter appointments.[1]

A 2016 meta-analysis found no hygiene or discomfort advantage for self-ligating brackets over conventional ones, and a 2016 review found no significant difference in periodontal status, according to Wikipedia's summary.[1] A 2010 review supported only shorter chair time and slightly less incisor proclination, while another analysis reported longer treatment times with self-ligating brackets.[1] A 2009 review found lower friction with small round wires in well-aligned arches but insufficient evidence for large rectangular wires.[1]

ClinicalTrials.gov lists a completed three-appliance trial (n=96, 2009 start) and a trial of Damon versus MBT brackets measuring compliance and treatment efficiency (n=34, active in 2025).[2][3] Results are not reported in the registry entries examined here. No trial examined whether Damon braces change facial structure.

Forum posters often present Damon braces as preferable to conventional braces and Invisalign for arch expansion and smile aesthetics, and some link them to jaw development, nasal breathing and "mewing".[4][5] Users commonly ask whether they affect the upper jaw (maxilla), with some replies saying they allow continued growth rather than directly changing the bone.[4]

lore.intro: Looksmax.org threads describe Damon braces as the best bracket type for arch widening and facial harmony, often alongside palate expanders.[4][5]

claims.claim: Damon braces widen the dental arch better than conventional braces or Invisalign.
Damon braces improve the maxilla or shift the jaw forward.
Damon braces are faster and more comfortable.

timeline.event: Damon 3 introduced as a metal and composite hybrid.[1]
